metadata.title: Can You Prove What Your Finance Agent Actually Did?
metadata.series: Humanitarians AI Fellows — Weekly Research Reports
metadata.source_status: Real fellow work, actual code and generated artifacts only (PR #17). SHA-256 proves file integrity, not identity, adequacy, or human approval. Recipe DRAFT; release BLOCKED_PENDING_HUMAN_REVIEW; five human gates open.

beats.narration_text: This is Onyx, in for Humanitarians AI. This week on the Mycroft Finance Investigator, the audit question. The investigator now has validated data, deterministic math, adversarial evaluations, scenario analysis, and an open review gate — but that evidence is scattered across dozens of files. So this week: can you package it into one bundle that proves every artifact came from the same investigation, and let a reviewer check it independently?

props.segment: Can You Prove What Your Finance Agent Actually Did?
props.command: The evidence is spread across dozens of files. How do you prove every artifact belongs to the same investigation — and let a reviewer verify it independently?
output: Validate the whole chain by hash first — run, review, evaluation, scenario, data.
Package 54 artifacts into one bundle: manifest.json, manifest.sha256, REVIEW.md.
verify-bundle recomputes every hash → INTEGRITY_MATCHED_HUMAN_REVIEW_OPEN. 41 tests, CI green.

props.title: The Scattered Proof
props.body: Validated data, deterministic math, adversarial evals, scenarios, an open review gate — all real, all in different files.

beats.narration_text: Each week added a real capability, and each one wrote its own files — logs, results, reports, hashes. Individually they're trustworthy. But a reviewer shouldn't have to take it on faith that this evaluation, that scenario, and this review request all describe the same run. Belonging has to be provable, not assumed.

props.sparkLine: Belonging must be provable, not assumed.
props.heading: One investigation, many files
props.body: Five kinds of evidence, spread across the repo. A reviewer needs one reproducible package that proves every artifact came from the same run.
props.evidenceNote: Integrity by hash, not by trust.

props.title: Validate, Then Package
props.body: bundle.py checks the whole chain by hash before it copies a single file.
props.sparkLine: Prove it before you pack it.

beats.narration_text: Before it packages anything, the bundle re-derives the links. The review request has to carry the same run ID and the same SHA-256 as the investigation log. The scenario output has to hash-match that baseline run and its plan. If any link is broken, packaging stops with an error. You cannot bundle evidence that doesn't provably belong together.

props.title: bundle.py — validate before packaging

beats.narration_text: Seven things have to line up before a single file is copied: the investigation run ID, the validation result, the review-request hash, the evaluation-case hash, the scenario-plan hash, the raw-data hashes, and the verified-data hashes. Miss one, and nothing gets packaged.

props.caption: All must match before anything is packaged.

beats.narration_text: Only then does it package — fifty-four artifacts in one folder. Raw and verified finance data, configuration, schemas, the implementation code, the tests, the investigation, evaluation, and scenario logs, the human-readable reports, the recipe, and the conductor. Alongside them, three integrity files: a manifest of every hash, a checksum of that manifest, and a human-readable REVIEW dot M-D.

artifactLines: Raw + verified data, config, schemas, implementation code, tests
Investigation, evaluation, scenario logs + human reports; recipe; conductor

props.title: Verify, Independently
props.body: verify-bundle recomputes every hash — it trusts nothing the packager wrote.

beats.narration_text: There's a separate command for the reviewer: verify-bundle. It re-reads the manifest and REVIEW checksums, recomputes the size and SHA-256 of every packaged artifact, and rejects any file that's extra, missing, or altered. When everything lines up, it prints one status: integrity matched, human review open.

artifactLines: Re-checks manifest + REVIEW.md checksums, then each artifact's size + SHA-256
Rejects any extra, missing, or altered file

beats.narration_text: And it's proven by trying to break it. Seven tamper cases, each rejected: an altered manifest, a modified reviewer view, a changed packaged artifact, an extra unlisted file, a mismatched run hash, an unsafe bundle name, and an overwrite attempt. Nine bundle tests in all, bringing the project to forty-one passing — and both GitHub CI checks green.

props.sparkLine: Seven ways to tamper — all caught.
props.caption: 9 bundle tests · 41 passing · both CI checks green.

beats.narration_text: But be precise about what this proves. A SHA-256 checksum proves file integrity — that these exact bytes have not changed since packaging. It does not prove identity. It does not prove the work is adequate. And it is not a human approval. The bundle even says so, in its own words.

props.heading: What a checksum proves
props.body: SHA-256 proves the exact bytes haven't changed. It does not prove identity, adequacy, or human approval.
props.evidenceNote: REVIEW.md: "an integrity checksum, not a signature, human attestation, or release approval."

beats.narration_text: So the bundle ships nothing. The recipe stays labeled DRAFT, the release status is blocked pending human review, and five gates stay visibly open: materiality approval, an evidence-backed causal explanation, evaluation adequacy, scenario approval, and distribution authorization. The machine packaged the proof. A named human still has to decide.

props.sparkLine: The machine packaged it. A human still decides.

beats.narration_text: The verdict. This week turns scattered evidence into an auditable package. The bundle validates the whole chain by hash — run, review, evaluation, scenario, and both raw and verified data — before packaging fifty-four artifacts with a manifest, a checksum, and a review file. An independent verify-bundle recomputes everything and reports integrity matched, human review open, with seven tamper cases rejected. SHA-256 proves integrity, not identity, adequacy, or approval — so the recipe stays DRAFT, the release stays blocked, and five human gates stay open.

artifactLines: bundle.py validates the whole chain by hash — run, review, evaluation, scenario, raw + verified data — before packaging.
54 artifacts in one folder with manifest.json, manifest.sha256, and REVIEW.md.
verify-bundle recomputes everything independently → INTEGRITY_MATCHED_HUMAN_REVIEW_OPEN; 7 tamper cases rejected.
SHA-256 proves file integrity — not identity, adequacy, or human approval.
Recipe DRAFT; release BLOCKED_PENDING_HUMAN_REVIEW; five gates open. 41 tests, CI green.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. An answer you can't reproduce isn't evidence — it's just a claim. So think about the tools you rely on, and answer in the comments: if an agent gives you an answer but cannot prove exactly which data, code, tests, and decisions produced it — can you really audit it?
